history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN TEMPLE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. TOWN CORRECTION: CSV lists the town as Bhavnagar, but the temple is at Palitana, Bhavnagar district - the Adinath temple atop Shatrunjaya hill, the principal shrine of the Palitana tirtha. Palitana is one of the holiest pilgrimage sites of Jainism (Svetambara tradition): Shatrunjaya hill ('the place of victory' / Shetrunjay) holds a complex of around 800-900 Jain temples clustered behind fortified walls, reached by climbing approx. 3,500-3,750 steps from Palitana town. The main Shri Adishwar/Adinath temple dedicated to Rishabhanatha (the first Tirthankara, called Adishwar/Adinath) is the heart of the complex. The tirtha's origins are legendary (associated with Adinath himself); the present temples were built and rebuilt over centuries, many in the 11th-19th centuries (verify precise chronology of the main shrine). Devotees climb the hill barefoot early in the morning; Palitana is a car-free, strictly vegetarian pilgrimage town. Coordinates (21.50508, 71.81423) are from mapcarta's 'Adishwar Pagla' on Shatrunjaya and mark the hill complex approximately; the exact main-shrine position is not independently verified.

name: Shri Adishwar Temple, Bhavnagar
town_description: Palitana is a temple town in Bhavnagar district, Gujarat, about 55 km southwest of Bhavnagar city, at the foot of Shatrunjaya hill. One of Jainism's holiest pilgrimage centres, it hosts hundreds of marble Jain temples on the hilltop and draws pilgrims and tourists from around the world, especially during the Kartik Purnima fair. Palitana is also famed as one of the world's first legally vegetarian cities. Nearby Bhavnagar offers further Jain and Hindu sites.

travel.airport: Bhavnagar Airport, approx. 55-65 km by road (verify); Ahmedabad approx. 215 km.
travel.railway: Palitana railway station (terminus on the Bhavnagar line); Bhavnagar Terminus approx. 55 km.
travel.road: Palitana is on the Ahmedabad-Palitana road, approx. 48-55 km from Bhavnagar and Dhola Junction; buses and taxis readily available. The hill complex itself is car-free - the only access is the climb of ~3,500 steps (palanquins available for the elderly).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when the weather suits the long early-morning climb; the Kartik Purnima fair is the most important and most crowded time.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Hill temples are typically open from early morning (around 6:00 AM) to evening; the climb takes 2-4 hours round trip - start early to avoid the heat (verify exact hours locally, as temple-managed timings are not consistently published). Palitana hill is a sacred Jain precinct: no entry fee reported (verify); modest dress, no leather goods or food on the hill, and non-Jain visitors should respect pilgrimage norms.
